notes: Exploratory soft-tissue hypotheses for Parasaurolophus sp. (RAM 14000). None of these values are dinosaur measurements; modifying or enabling them cannot upgrade a bone-derived profile above EXPLORATORY.

mucosa_thickness_mm.model_source: Steiner inward parallel offset A_lumen = A_bone - P_bone*t + pi*t^2
mucosa_thickness_mm.notes: Brackets the unsourced 2.0 mm lining_thickness_mm prior from step-2 metadata.json. Uniform t along s is a geometric sensitivity assumption on a bone-derived profile, not a lumen reconstruction. Above ~2.8 mm, the narrowest anterior bone cross-section occludes.

wall_mass_per_area.model_source: Ishizaka, K., French, J. C., & Flanagan, J. L. (1975). Direct determination of vocal tract wall impedance. IEEE Trans. ASSP, 23(4), 370-373. DOI: 10.1109/TASSP.1975.1162701; Sondhi, M. M. (1974). Model for wave propagation in a lossy vocal tract. J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 55(5), 1070-1075. DOI: 10.1121/1.1914649
wall_mass_per_area.notes: Effective mucosal/perimural surface mass density per unit wall area. Order of magnitude unknown in an ossified hadrosaur crest surrounded by thin mucosa; spans 1.4 decades [2, 50] kg/m^2 (geometric mean 10 kg/m^2) bracketing soft-to-stiffened tissue.

wall_stiffness_per_area.model_source: Ishizaka, K., French, J. C., & Flanagan, J. L. (1975). Direct determination of vocal tract wall impedance. IEEE Trans. ASSP, 23(4), 370-373. DOI: 10.1109/TASSP.1975.1162701; Sondhi, M. M. (1974). Model for wave propagation in a lossy vocal tract. J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 55(5), 1070-1075. DOI: 10.1121/1.1914649
wall_stiffness_per_area.notes: Effective wall stiffness per unit area K_w (Pa/m = N/m^3). Unknown for mucosa backed by rigid crest bone; spans two decades [1e5, 1e7] Pa/m (geometric mean 1e6 Pa/m) from compliant soft tissue toward bone-backed mucosa.

wall_resistance_per_area.model_source: Ishizaka, K., French, J. C., & Flanagan, J. L. (1975). Direct determination of vocal tract wall impedance. IEEE Trans. ASSP, 23(4), 370-373. DOI: 10.1109/TASSP.1975.1162701; Sondhi, M. M. (1974). Model for wave propagation in a lossy vocal tract. J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 55(5), 1070-1075. DOI: 10.1121/1.1914649
wall_resistance_per_area.notes: Specific wall mechanical resistance R_w (Pa*s/m). Order of magnitude unknown; spans 1.6 decades [500, 20000] Pa*s/m (geometric mean ~3162 Pa*s/m).

extra_damping_factor.model_source: Kirchhoff, G. (1868); Keefe, D. H. (1984). Acoustical wave propagation in cylindrical ducts. J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 75(1), 58-62. DOI: 10.1121/1.390300
extra_damping_factor.notes: Dimensionless multiplier (>= 1.0) on smooth-wall Kirchhoff thermoviscous attenuation alpha to represent surface roughness, mucus film, and non-circular corner losses (1.0 = smooth dry rigid baseline, up to 3.0x).

f0_prior_hz.model_source: Steinecke, I., & Herzel, H. (1995). Bifurcations in an asymmetric vocal-fold model. J. Acoust. Soc. Am., 97(3), 1874-1884. DOI: 10.1121/1.412061
f0_prior_hz.notes: Unobserved glottal/syringeal fundamental frequency prior spanning one octave below and above the legacy 60 Hz assumption [30, 120] Hz (geometric mean 60.0 Hz).

air_temperature_c.model_source: Ideal-gas sound speed and Sutherland air viscosity (TMM Air.from_temperature)
air_temperature_c.notes: Airway gas temperature is unknown; 20 C represents ambient room-air baseline and 37 C represents an endotherm-like physiological scenario, not a paleobiological measurement. Midpoint 28.5 C is used only as nominal midpoint when sweeping.

lumen_min_area_fraction.notes: Geometric validity guard: any inward offset leaving < 5% of bone area (or <= 0 area/perimeter) raises SoftTissueError as an occluded lumen.
